To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a combination of 3 pre-trained CNNs, trained on different pre-processing regimes, can be used to accurately classify histology images of breast cancer.

a) an ensemble of 3 CNNs, trained on different data normalization schemes, achieves an accuracy of 88% on the challenge data and b) an accuracy of 95% can be achieved on a larger data set (n 40), which includes the challenge data.

a combination of 3 CNNs pre trained using different pre processing regimes and data normalization techniques, achieves a high accuracy on a held out test set and is competitive with other algorithms in the field of classification of histology images.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of ensemble of CNN to classify breast cancer histology images.
the classification of breast cancer histology image into Normal, In situ (DCIS), Benign (LCIS) and Invasive.
the development of a technique to classify histology image into 4 categories and the proposed technique is adjudged as one of the top performers on the challenge data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed technique is a robust and efficient scheme for the classification of breast cancer histopathology images and could be used for the diagnosis of breast cancer in a clinical setting.
ensemble of CNNs trained on data pre processed using different normalization schemes is a promising technique for the classification of breast cancer histology images.
ensemble of pre trained CNNs is the best performing scheme for classification of breast cancer histology images.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that a combination of multiple CNNs can be used to classify histology image as Normal, In Situ, Benign or invasive.

we were able to achieve the state of the art performance on the data provided for the challenge and we were also able to achieve a performance comparable to the best performing algorithm on the held out test set.
we have developed a technique to classify histology image as Normal, In Situ, Benign and Invasive with an accuracy of 85% and 97.5%, on the challenge data and held out data, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
an ensemble of multiple CNN architectures trained on multiple pre processing regimes is a viable approach for the problem of histology image classification.

the performance of CNN is highly dependent on data normalization and that a combination of CNNs trained on multiple data normalization schemes is likely to perform better than a single network trained on a single pre processing regime.
an ensemble of CNNs trained on data preprocessed using different schemes can achieve superior performance compared to the performance of individual models trained on the same data.
